verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT local time), in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R4: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm exact date, time (equivalent across time zones), and location.

verifications.claim: The splashdown occurred at 0007 GMT on April 11.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct match to UTC/GMT time in primary source.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew included Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Crew size 4 Members Reid Wiseman Victor Glover Christina Koch Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list repeated across sources.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew concluded a 10-day mission.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds'; R2: '10-day mission'; R4: 'approximate 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Precisely ~9 days 1.5 hours, but commonly described as 10-day mission; rounded approximation.

verifications.claim: Artemis II marked the first human return from the Moon since 1972.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'crewed lunar flyby... first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972'; no landing or return from lunar surface
verifications.reasoning: Flyby, not landing/return from Moon surface; Apollo 17 was last surface mission.

verifications.claim: The landing occurred on Friday, April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Date/time confirmed; day 'Friday' stated in R3.

verifications.claim: The landing location was the Pacific Ocean near San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'; R2: 'off California’s coast'; R3: 'off the coast of San Diego'

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration was 10 days.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R2: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Exact duration slightly under 10 days; commonly approximated as 10 days.

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft separated from the service module at 7:33 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'service module will separate around 7:33 p.m.'; R4: '7:33 p.m.'

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft separated from the service module to prepare for atmospheric reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'service module will separate... before Orion reaches the upper atmosphere'; R4: 'crew module continues... service module will harmlessly burn up'

verifications.claim: The Orion spacecraft endured temperatures of ~3,000°F.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: The crew was extracted by NASA and U.S. Navy teams following splashdown
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'U.S. Navy recovered the crew'; R2: 'NASA and U.S. Navy team'; R4: 'NASA and U.S. military team'
